report:
In the medial compartment, there is complex tear (main radial component) at the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is displaced meniscal fragment into the medial gutter. There is diffuse high grade and low grade chondrosis (less than and more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along weightbaring medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. There is no subchondral edema. Osteophytes are present. 
  
 The lateral compartment, there is complex tear with buckethandle tear at the anterior horn, body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is focal high grade chondrosis at the the posterolateral tibial plateau (about 1.5* 1.9 cm). There is subchondral edema. Osteophytes are present.  
  
 The patellofemoral joint, there is focal grade  chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at the medial patellar facet (about 1.3* 1 cm). The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is no tibial translation. 
  
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
  
 Minimal amount of right knee effusion is present.The surrounding musculature is normal.  Mild medial tibiofemoral compartmental osteoarthritis of the right knee by evidence of chondrosis, subchondral edema and osteophytes. 
  Focal high grade chondrosis at the the posterolateral tibial plateau (about 1.5* 1.9 cm).  
  Focal low grade  chondrosis at the medial patellar facet (about 1.3* 1 cm).  
  Complex tear (main radial component) at the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. (note: displaced meniscal fragment into the medial gutter). 
  Complex tear with buckethandle tear at the anterior horn, body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. 
  Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance.  
  Minimal amount of right knee effusion.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
No significant joint effusion. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Moderate to severe degeneration. Diffuse partial thickness chondral loss with full-thickness chondral loss of the weightbearing portion of the compartment. Minimal associated subchondral reactive marrow change. Marginal osteophytes.
Complex multidirectional tear of the posterior horn and body of the meniscus with a dominant radial component involving the posterior root horn junction. Associated meniscal substance loss. Early flap tear with mild displacement into the tibial gutter. Mild extrusion of the body.
Medial collateral imaging is intact.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Moderate to severe degeneration.
Diffuse high-grade partial-thickness chondral loss with no full-thickness component. Marginal osteophytosis.
Complex multidirectional tear of the posterior horn and body of the meniscus with a horizontal oblique longitudinal components and meniscal substance loss. Mild meniscal extrusion.
The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
The ACL and PCL are intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Moderate to severe degeneration.
Full thickness chondral loss of the inferior aspect of the lateral and medial facets with subchondral reactive marrow change, full-thickness chondral loss of the lateral facet of the trochlea, and diffuse high-grade partial thickness chondral loss of the medial facet.
Marginal osteophytosis. Mild edema of the suprapatellar fat pad.

Bones:
See above.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
Small ganglion cyst seen posterior to the PCL measuring up to 7 mm.

CONCLUSION:
1.Moderate to severe tricompartmental degenerative disease.
2.Complex multidirectional tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with a dominant radial component involving the posterior root horn junction. Associated meniscal substance loss. Early flap tear with mild displacement into the tibial gutter.
3.Complex multidirectional tear of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus with a horizontal oblique longitudinal components and meniscal substance loss. Mild meniscal extrusion.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Lateral knee pain.
Comparison: Right knee radiograph [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.2 Tesla open system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Small leaking Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear involving the body, posterior horn and posterior root, noting a complete radial tear at the posterior root. Moderate meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint with areas of full-thickness cartilage loss/fissuring and associated subchondral signal changes.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint in the lateral joint line.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade articular cartilage loss throughout the patella with areas of full-thickness loss at the median ridge and medial facet with associated subchondral signal changes.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon. Stripping of the prepatellar quadriceps continuation. Prepatellar bursitis.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 12 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body, posterior horn and posterior root. Dominant complete radial component at the posterior root. Moderate meniscal extrusion.
2.	Mild-to-moderate tricompartmental osteoarthritis. Moderate knee joint effusion.
3.	Small leaking Baker's cyst.
4.	Prepatellar bursitis.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Medial joint pain for 20 years, no known cause. No surgical history.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Area of full-thickness chondrosis along the posterior weightbearing medial femoral condyle extending to the posterior nonweightbearing condyle with subchondral bone marrow edema and cystic change. The tibial plateau is within normal limits.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Focal full-thickness fissuring at the posterolateral tibial plateau with subchondral cystic change.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness fissuring at the medial patellar facet with subchondral edema. Low-grade fissuring at the junction of the lateral facet and median ridge. Focal full-thickness fissuring along the inferomedial trochlea with subchondral cystic change.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal tendinosis with insertional enthesopathy.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Mild lateral patellar translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 12 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1. Tricompartmental chondrosis, moderate in the medial compartment.

2. No acute osseous, ligamentous or meniscal injury.

Mediales Kompartiment:
Osteophytäre Anbauten an der medialen Femurcondyle. Vollständig fehlender Knorpelbesatz in der Belastungszone an der medialen Femurcondyle sowie fokal vollschichtige Knorpeldefekte in der tibialen Belastungszone mit angrenzend deutlichem subchondralem Knochenödem. Geringes subchondrales Knochenödem an der medialen Femurcondyle. Komplexe Rissbildung mit kleiner Lappenkomponente in der Pars intermedia und dem Hinterhorn des Innenmeniskus mit radiärer und vertikaler Komponente (Serie 3/ Image 116, Serie 4/ Image 24) bei deutlicher mukoider Auffaserung. Intaktes MCL.

Laterales Kompartiment:
Osteophytäre Anbuaten an der lateralen Femurcondyle. Fokal vollschichtiger 5 x 6 mm messender Knorpeldefekt in der dorsalen Belastungszone der lateralen Femurcondyle mit geringem angrenzendem subchondralem Knochenödem (Serie 4/ Image 25). Geringe mukoide Degeneration im Außenmeniskushinterhorn. Intaktes LCL.

Femoropatellares Gleitlager und Trochlea:
Geringe Lateralisierung der Patella. Oberflächliche Knorpelirregularitäten retropatellar und trochleär mit teils auch tieferen Einrissen und subchondraler Zystenbildung an der lateralen Patellafacette sowie an der Trochlea beidseits (Serie 3/ Image 38). Regelrechte Darstellung der Quadrizeps- und Patellarsehne. Regelrechte Darstellung des Hoffa`schen Fettkörpers.

Kreuzbänder:
Intakte Kreuzbänder.

Muskulatur und übrige Weichteile:
Geringer Gelenkerguss mit verdickter Synovia und synovialen Proliferationen. Flüssigkeitsgefüllte Baker-Zyste.
